ai.name: Moonshot AI
ai.hook: Kimi K3 demand is so high Moonshot **suspended new subscriptions** entirely.
insights: K3 leads the **Frontend Code Arena** with a 76% pairwise win rate, beating Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol
Model is **2.8T params, 1M context**, open weights promised by **July 27, 2026**
New attention mechanism (**Kimi Delta Attention**) gives **6.3x faster decoding**
ai.for_you: When weights drop July 27, worth testing K3 against whatever you're using for the agency's coding/agentic client work, if it's genuinely Sonnet-class at open-weight pricing that changes your cost stack for PT SMB projects.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Real demand signal (suspended signups), not just benchmark hype, escalation of a story already tracked

ai.name: Nathan Lambert
ai.hook: Calls this the **most serious test yet** of whether open source AI can survive near the frontier.
insights: Argues the strategic battle has shifted from **compute moat to efficiency stack**: MoE routing, quantization, data curation
Zyphra, Cohere, and Poolside are all expanding what counts as "open" beyond just weights
GLM-5.2 marks a capability threshold for open agents specifically
ai.for_you: If open models keep closing the gap on agentic coding, your agency's cost argument to PT SMBs gets stronger, you can pitch open-weight-powered automations instead of routing everything through expensive closed APIs.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most substantive strategic framing of the open-vs-closed story this week

ai.name: Thinking Machines Lab
ai.hook: Ships **Inkling**, its first open-weights model family, undercutting closed rivals on cost.
insights: 975B params with only **41B active** (MoE), Apache 2.0 licensed
Supports **text, image, audio input** with 1M context window
Immediate ecosystem support: vLLM, SGLang, Modal, Baseten, Databricks day one
ai.for_you: Apache 2.0 licensing means no legal ambiguity for commercial use, worth a bench test if you ever need a local/self-hosted multimodal option for a PT client wary of sending data to US clouds.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only fully open, commercially-clean frontier-adjacent release this cycle

ai.name: Andrej Karpathy
ai.hook: Says there are things you **literally can't say** inside a frontier AI lab.
insights: Argues lab employment structurally limits acting as an independent agent
Points to unresolved founding tension at OpenAI as a recurring pattern across labs
ai.for_you: No direct action here, filed for awareness, it's a useful mental model for reading lab announcements skeptically (including today's Kimi/Inkling hype) rather than taking them at face value.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Karpathy's most quoted line this week per No Priors engagement

ai.name: Lila Sciences (Andy Beam & Rafa Gómez-Bombarelli)
ai.hook: The wet lab becomes the **verifier**, turning science itself into reinforcement learning.
insights: One general model trained on ~10 trillion experimentally-verified tokens beats domain-specific ones: **"breadth gives us depth"**
A CAR-T candidate was designed in six months by **two or three people**
"Zero-FTE startup" model: the lab isn't the product, the model is
ai.for_you: No direct action here, filed for awareness, but the RL-with-real-world-verifier pattern (versus synthetic reward hacking) is worth remembering if you ever build an agentic workflow for the agency that needs a trustworthy ground truth signal.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most conceptually novel podcast this week, genuinely new framing on RL beyond chat

ai.name: MIT Technology Review
ai.hook: New research shows LLMs can develop **their own hiring biases**, beyond what they inherit from training data.
insights: Researchers found bias emerging independent of human-labeled training data patterns
Raises direct concern for any resume-screening or candidate-matching product
ai.for_you: Relevant if the agency ever pitches an HR/recruiting automation to a PT SMB client, flag this as a liability talking point before you ship anything screening real candidates.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only genuinely new research finding today, not a product launch

build_this.name: verifiers v1 (Prime Intellect)
build_this.what_it_is: A redesigned agentic RL environment stack that stores rollout traces as message DAGs, cutting complexity from O(n²) to O(n).
build_this.why_try_it: If you're prototyping an agentic workflow for a client (multi-turn task execution, not just single-shot prompts), this is the kind of harness worth studying, since Pedro isn't yet a developer, at minimum read the repo to understand what "good agent infrastructure" looks like before you evaluate agency tooling vendors.

build_this.name: Claude Code + Bun/Rust rewrite writeup
build_this.what_it_is: Simon Willison verifies Claude Code now runs on a Rust port of Bun for a 10% faster startup, and shows exactly how to check this yourself with shell commands.
build_this.why_try_it: A quick, low-effort exercise to sharpen your technical fluency this week: run the `strings` command he shows on your own Claude Code install, it's a concrete, 5-minute way to build the habit of verifying tool internals instead of trusting release notes.

build_this.name: PostHog
build_this.what_it_is: Open-source product analytics platform now positioned around AI agent observability (session replay, error tracking, feature flags, MCP support).
build_this.why_try_it: Worth wiring into the yoga/meditation platform now while it's still small, so you have real usage data (drop-off points, session replays) before you scale it, and it doubles as a reference stack you could recommend to PT SMB clients building their own products.

podcasts.episode: How a Writer Uses AI Without Losing His Voice
podcasts.takeaway: Craig Mod rebuilt his own newsletter tool with AI and cut a $7,000/year vendor bill to $150.
key_points: He calls this a "golden age of tool building" where anyone can build software fitted exactly to their needs
He draws a hard line: uses AI to build tools, refuses to use it to write
Keeps a tech-free zone in the mornings specifically to protect deep thinking
podcasts.for_you: This is almost exactly your micro-SaaS thesis, a solo builder replacing an expensive SaaS subscription with a custom AI-built tool, worth listening for the specific build decisions he made, not just the inspiration.
